summary: R1: testCount now sums cargo's test result lines, reads jest's Tests: line and counts go -v's --- PASS lines (node:test and generic as before); five runner fixtures in tests/fixtures/check-*.txt; run_init notes `test count: no match in the suite's output (tests start/end stay unknown)` once per run. Decision file, architecture.md and README updated.
verified_how: Fixtures generated in scratch: `node --test` (v24.21.0, 3 tests), `~/.local/bin/pytest -p no:cacheprovider` (9.1.1, 4 tests), `cargo test --offline` (1.99.0, 2 unit + 1 doc-test); jest and go copied from getSummary.ts / testing.go (fetched, formats confirmed). Red first: on main's testcount the 5 unit checks gave node 3, pytest 4, jest 7 PASS, cargo `1 tests` and go nothing FAIL; the no-match check FAILed on main's driver (run-1 + scratch subset, 39/40). After: subset 40/40; with the once-per-run marker removed the check FAILs (nocount noted twice). Full suite through check.sh: green in 615 s, 331/331 checks passed.

dead_ends.why: a continue with a list and a past deadline runs no run_init, so it can't show once-per-run across segments; the second segment now runs the stub features to the end

discoveries.text: This repo's own suite prints `N/M checks passed`, which no rule matches (`checks` isn't `tests`), so agent-harness runs will get the `test count: no match` note and `? → ?` until tests/run.sh prints e.g. `N tests passed` or a rule for it is added
Every stub run now has one `test count: no match` line in harness-log.md (the stub suite `test ! -f BROKEN` prints nothing); no existing check counted harness-log lines exactly

questions: D2/D3 defaults (in decisions/2026-10-26-real-test-counts): empty suite output also gets the no-match note, and go is counted only from `go test -v`'s --- PASS lines. Keep both?
Should tests/run.sh's last line say `N tests passed` so this repo's own runs get a real count?
